article_limitations: Disposition aggregate_only: the source is a retrospective single-centre series of 10 patients (9 women, 1 man) who underwent LAMS-induced removal of non-eroding silastic bands, reported only as means, medians, ranges, counts and percentages; no patient has individual identity evidence or an individually described course, so no individual patient records are created and cohort statements are not copied to placeholder patients.
reported_individual_count is 10 (literal) and roster_complete is false because none of the 10 stated individuals can be enumerated.

Singleton subgroups are each described by a single attribute and are not individuated: the one man, the one patient with a mechanical mitral valve who was hospitalized two weeks after the procedure with suspected endocarditis and treated with antibiotics, and the two patients with persistent but improved emesis who gained weight and refused further endoscopic dilatation. The source never links these subgroups to one another or to any other attribute (for example, whether the endocarditis patient is one of the four who needed balloon dilatation), so no link is inferred.

Table 3 is printed with a malformed header: the first row reads "Emesis present, n (%) | Pre-procedure | Post-procedure" with a single data row "10 (100%) | 2 (20%)". The text states emesis was present in all 10 patients before and persisted in 2 patients (20%) at follow-up, so the cells are read that way, but the table layout itself does not label which value is which.

Table 1 lists Gastric stenosis in 10 (100%) patients before stent placement, while Table 2 and the text describe four patients who developed gastric stenosis (re-stenosis) after band removal and needed balloon dilation; these are different time points and are not reconciled as one measurement.

The abstract says all patients were discharged within 24 h, while the methods and discussion say the procedures were outpatient and patients could be discharged the same day, and one patient was hospitalized two weeks after the procedure; these refer to different encounters and are recorded as printed.
The Eckardt score is described as including weight measured in kilograms, but the source does not give its components or the individual scores; only the cohort means are printed.

Figures 1 and 2 are endoscopic images whose patient is not identified in the caption; panel ownership is unresolved. Fig. 2a is captioned as two months after insertion, which is a caption claim for that image only, not a time for any individual patient.
No supplementary material is listed in the source (raw.xml has no supplementary-material element and source.json lists no supplements or unassigned media).
